excerpts:
1:01 PM EDT on July 2, 2024 Add Relix to Google Jason Galea King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard has taken to its social channels to announce Flight b741 , the band’s hotly-anticipated 26th studio album. Set to fly from p(doom)–the group’s recently established independent record label–on August 9, the latest offering is still shrouded in intrigue, with no release accompanying its first announcement; fans will have to hold out until July 9 for the first single and an accompanying music video directed by Guy Tyzack, who previously created the video for “Black Hot Soup” from King Gizzard’s acclaimed leftfield 2021 project Butterfly 3000 . results.title: King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard Announce New Album
excerpts: The prolific Australian prog-rockers are back with a new orchestral LP, following 2024’s ‘Flight B741’, arriving on their (P)Doom label By Sarah Downs King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard Maclay Heriot King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard are back at it again, this time with the announcement of Phantom Island , their 27th studio album. Following the release of Flight B741 last year, the prolific Australian prog-rock band teased the orchestral LP, confirming it was recorded alongside their 2024 album in a two-year project. The title track has dropped, alongside the cover art, but fans will need to hold tight for a full release date – more info is set to land on April 15th. You can check it out below. results.title: King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard Are Releasing an EDM Album | Pitchfork
excerpts: Watch the video for “Level 5” from Alien Metal By Jazz Monroe July 8, 2026 Photo by Maclay Heriot Save this story Save this story After an uncharacteristically long break of 13 months since their last studio LP, King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard have announced a new album. Set to arrive “later in the summer” (sure, who needs release dates), Alien Metal marks the band’s foray into EDM, a press release notes. A new song, “Level 5,” presents compelling evidence for the claim. Watch the Hayden Somerville-directed video, in which some sort of cabal performs freaky electronic surgery on an unsuspecting patient, below. Today’s news is pegged to the Melbourne sextet’s forthcoming three-night stint at New York’s Forest Hills Stadium next month. Skip to main content Open
